- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 75+ → forecast jumps to 78+).
- Underestimates in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days of 30d), suggesting lag or mean reversion bias.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true outcomes, missing volatility or sudden drops.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model fails to fully capture the momentum, underestimating peak values.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent highs.
- Correction should reduce forecast by 1–3% for late-period days and adjust downward after spikes.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends; consider mean reversion if history shows divergence from recent mean.
